Plume is a feather-light Markdown viewer. Double-click a `.md` file and it opens straight into a clean reading view: no workspace to import, no project to set up, no editor chrome.

**1.9.0 opens where you left off.**

1.8.0 gave notes somewhere to live, and then asked you where that was every
time you launched it. Plume now comes back into the vault it was last in, on
the note it was last showing. Which note that is, is remembered inside the
vault itself and never leaves the computer it was read on, so a laptop and a
desktop on the same vault each come back to their own place in it.

The chooser is still what a new install opens on, and what **Manage vaults…**
goes back to. It is no longer the door you walk through twice a day.

**Making a vault asks what it is called before it asks where it goes.** It used
to open a folder dialog, which can only ask *where* — so the vault was named
after whatever folder you found, and making a new folder meant finding the New
Folder button inside someone else's dialog. Now there are two questions on one
screen, Plume makes the folder itself with the name you typed, and a line
underneath says exactly which folder is about to appear.

**A new vault opens on a note rather than on nothing.** It is given a
`Welcome.md` to start from, which you delete once you have your own. Claiming a
folder that already holds Markdown still writes nothing into it but `.plume/` —
the notes that were already there are what it opens on.

**The bar at the foot of the sidebar is the list of vaults.** Press the name
and they are all there, the one you are in ticked, with your account and
**Manage vaults…** underneath. Help and settings sit at the far end of the bar.
The separate switcher button is gone, and **Ctrl+Shift+V** still opens the same
list.

Opening a vault, switching to one, claiming a folder as one and downloading one
from your account all now land you *in* it, on a note, rather than reporting
that something happened.
